new_statements.rule_in_words: The author treats stress as non-contrastive in Siraji, characterises the language as syllable-timed, and recognises stress only as emphatic prominence placed on whole words in an utterance; no default word-internal stress position is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None. (Same chapter, 2.2.5: sentence intonation nucleus 'usually positioned on the penultimate word or on negative particle'.)
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word/utterance level in general; no citation-form stress position is described anywhere in the thesis. Independent first-hand data point: Schmidt & Kaul 2008 (Acta Orientalia 69, Table 3) transcribe a recorded 267-item Siraji (Kashtigarh, Doda) list with 'stress on first syllable unless otherwise noted' and mark many items with non-initial stress (kasa:'li:, tsu'tsu, mu'tar, ka:l'zo, phak'ku, re'ti:, ma:'li:), i.e. audible word prominence that is not uniformly initial, but they state no rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sira1263 'Sirajic' is a language-level node whose two dialects are sira1264 'Siraji of Doda' (= Sarazi/Sirazi/Siraji, Saraz belt of Doda, Ramban and Kishtwar districts) and ramb1240 'Rambani'. The quoted source (Mushtaq 2020) describes Siraji = Sarazi (sira1264), with data recorded in Neera village, Ramban district (inside the Saraz belt, not Grierson's Rambani). Parihar 2019 describes Sarazi of the Jodhpur area, Doda district (also sira1264). No modern description of Rambani (ramb1240) was found beyond Bailey 1908 and Grierson 1919. Not to be confused with Inner/Outer Siraji of Kullu, Himachal (Western Pahari, different glottocodes).

No default position given. 2.2.5 Intonation: sentence intonation 'usually positioned on the penultimate word or on negative particle'. Data from Neera village, Ramban district.

sources.citation: Ravi Parihar. 2019. A Linguistic Grammar of the Sarazi Language. PhD thesis, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, Katra (supervisor Amitabh Vikram Dwivedi). Shodhganga, hdl.handle.net/10603/342722. (Basis of Parihar & Dwivedi 2019, A Grammar of Sarazi, LINCOM.)
sources.note: Ch. 4 'The phonological analysis of the Sarazi sounds' (pp. 137-172): introduction lists 'suprasegmental features such as nasalization, length, and stress', but the chapter treats only consonants, vowels, nasalization, length, syllable structure, clusters and PRAAT spectrograms; stress is never described. Silent on stress placement.

sources.note: Explicitly segmental (31 consonants, 13 vowels, diphthongs, clusters, syllable types, gemination); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Anton I. Kogan. 2012. Nekotorye problemy kashmirskoj dialektologii [Some issues of Kashmiri dialectology]. Journal of Language Relationship / Voprosy jazykovogo rodstva 7: 47-70.
sources.note: Historical-comparative phonology arguing Siraji and Rambani are not Kashmiri/Dardic; nothing on stress. Fn. 15 notes Schmidt & Kaul's rising-tone marks on vowels next to historical voiced aspirates and speculates on incipient positional tone. Lists the then-available descriptions (Bailey, Grierson, P. K. Koul 1977/2006, Schmidt & Kaul 2008).

sources.citation: Ruth Laila Schmidt & Vijay Kumar Kaul. 2008. A comparative analysis of Shina and Kashmiri vocabularies. Acta Orientalia 69: 231-302. doi 10.5617/ao.7372.
sources.note: Table 3 (pp. 283ff) includes a 267-item Siraji (Kashtigarh, Doda) list transcribed from recordings with the convention 'Stress on first syllable unless otherwise noted'; many Siraji items carry an explicit non-initial stress mark (e.g. kasa:'li: 'armpit', ha'ḍi: 'bone', tsu'tsu 'breast', mu'tar 'urine', ka:l'zo 'liver', phak'ku 'shoulder', re'ti: 'daughter', ma:'li: 'mother'). No stress rule is stated for Siraji; p. 235 says Kashmiri is syllable-timed and Kashtawari/Poguli 'appear to be', without extending this to Siraji; p. 233 'A rising tone was occasionally heard in Siraji words'.

sources.citation: George A. Grierson. 1919. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. VIII part II (Dardic or Pisacha languages, including Kashmiri): 'Siraji of Doda' pp. 432-457, 'Rambani' pp. 458-487. Calcutta.
sources.note: 'Pronunciation' subsections (vowels, consonants) for Siraji and Rambani; no statement on accent or stress.
